paper_id: Liu et al. - 2011 - Self-diagnosis for large scale wireless sensor networks
title: Self-Diagnosis for Large Scale Wireless Sensor Networks
motivation: sink-based diagnosis incurs huge communication overhead; sink often gets incomplete/suspicious info; problematic regions hardest to query
problem_framing: self-diagnosis: each sensor joins fault decision; multiple nodes cooperate via FSM-based fault detectors encoding state transitions
key_insight: fault detectors travel among nodes, each contributing local evidence to transit state; when sufficient evidence accumulates, detector reaches Accept state
method_signature: FSM-based fault detectors with state transitions driven by local node evidence; diagnosis triggered via CUSUM+bootstrap change-point detection
evaluation_criteria: detection ratio (% faults caught) and false alarm ratio across 20-100 node networks, compared with PAD
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: currently our fault detectors are deterministic, and in future works we plan to extend our model to cope with non-deterministic cases
evidence_for_taste: fault detectors encode the diagnosis process
thinking_moves: 把 sink pull 模型翻转为节点 push 自诊断
用 FSM 状态机编码诊断推理过程
多节点局部证据聚合成全局诊断结论
把异常触发条件形式化为变点检测问题
先定性 FSM 可行, 再经验调参 bootstrap 阈值
